**Part A:**
Let $S = \{1, \dots, 5000\}$.
First, find the number of integers divisible by at least one of 6, 10, 15 using the principle of inclusion-exclusion:
- Multiples of 6: $\lfloor 5000 / 6 \rfloor = 833$
- Multiples of 10: $\lfloor 5000 / 10 \rfloor = 500$
- Multiples of 15: $\lfloor 5000 / 15 \rfloor = 333$
- Multiples of $\text{lcm}(6, 10) = 30$: $\lfloor 5000 / 30 \rfloor = 166$
- Multiples of $\text{lcm}(6, 15) = 30$: $\lfloor 5000 / 30 \rfloor = 166$
- Multiples of $\text{lcm}(10, 15) = 30$: $\lfloor 5000 / 30 \rfloor = 166$
- Multiples of $\text{lcm}(6, 10, 15) = 30$: $\lfloor 5000 / 30 \rfloor = 166$

Total divisible by at least one of 6, 10, 15:
$N = 833 + 500 + 333 - 166 - 166 - 166 + 166 = 1168$.

Now, subtract those that are also divisible by 13:
- Divisible by $\text{lcm}(6, 13) = 78$: $\lfloor 5000 / 78 \rfloor = 64$
- Divisible by $\text{lcm}(10, 13) = 130$: $\lfloor 5000 / 130 \rfloor = 38$
- Divisible by $\text{lcm}(15, 13) = 195$: $\lfloor 5000 / 195 \rfloor = 25$
- Divisible by $\text{lcm}(30, 13) = 390$: $\lfloor 5000 / 390 \rfloor = 12$ (this covers pairs and the triple of 6, 10, 15 with 13)

By inclusion-exclusion for multiples of 13:
$N_{13} = 64 + 38 + 25 - 12 - 12 - 12 + 12 = 127 - 24 = 101$ (since $64 + 38 + 25 - 3(12) + 12 = 101$).

Thus, the count is $1168 - 101 = 1067$.
